messages.content: Can you fetch the server's response if I send a GET request to 'https://api.intent.com/query' with the following queries to recognize their corresponding intents: [hello, I want to transfer funds, show my balance, hey there]? The list of intent-codes is [get_balance, transfer_funds, hello, goodbye].

function.name: get_response
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to the specified URL and retrieves the server's response. This is typically used for API calls and web content fetching. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. Must be a valid HTTP or HTTPS endpoint, such as 'https://api.example.com/data'.

intents.description: A list of intent codes derived from user queries, represented as strings. For example, ['weather', 'news'].

timeout.description: The maximum time, in seconds, to wait for the server's response before the request times out. For example, a timeout of 30.0 seconds. This is a float type value.

User-Agent.description: The User-Agent header's value representing the client software identity, such as 'MyApp/1.0'.

Accept.description: The Accept header's value indicating the media types which are acceptable for the response, like 'application/json'.

headers.description: Optional HTTP headers to include in the request. If not provided, default headers will be used.

The user wants us to fetch the server's response. We need to call the get_response function. Provide the URL, intents array, maybe timeout. Also we can provide headers? Not necessary. We'll pass intents: ['hello', 'I want to transfer funds', 'show my balance', 'hey there']. But the function expects "intents" param to be a list of intent codes derived from user queries. Wait reading the function description: "A list of intent codes derived from user queries". So we should pass the list of intent codes recognized from the queries. The user gave list of intent-codes: [get_balance, transfer_funds, hello, goodbye]. But they didn't specify mapping. They just said "list of intent-codes is [get_balance, transfer_funds, hello, goodbye]". That might mean we should use those as possible intents. But the function expects the actual intents recognized from queries. Possibly we should pass the list of intent codes recognized from the queries: e.g., ['hello', 'transfer_funds', 'get_balance', 'hello']? Actually the queries: [hello, I want to transfer funds, show my balance, hey there]. Recognized intents: hello -> hello; I want to transfer funds -> transfer_funds; show my balance -> get_balance; hey there -> hello (maybe). So the list would be ['hello', 'transfer_funds', 'get_balance', 'hello']. But the user also says "The list of intent-codes is [get_balance, transfer_funds, hello, goodbye]". That might be the set of possible intents. But the function expects the recognized ones. So we should pass the recognized ones.

Thus we call get_response with url: 'https://api.intent.com/query', intents: ['hello', 'transfer_funds', 'get_balance', 'hello'], maybe timeout: 30.0. No custom headers needed.

We then output the result.
